name: acceptance
definition: any variety of a bill of exchange, inland bill, draft, or other financial instrument that has been accepted by the payer as a legitimate claim upon its assets but is not yet paid because the instrument has not yet matured or has not yet been presented for payment

name: accept
definition: to agree to pay a bill of exchange, inland bill, draft, or other financial instrument according to its usance

name: account books
definition: books (or papers or computer files) where accounts are maintained

name: accounts
definition: a record of debits and/or credits maintained by an entity in its account books

name: actuarial
definition: the condition or state of being created by an actuary

name: actuary
definition: an entity that computes insurance risks and premiums in a scientifically and statistically valid way

name: acquisition
definition: the purchase, takeover, and balance sheet consolidation of one business entity by another, typically larger surviving entity

name: adverse selection
definition: a type of asymmetric information whereby the highest risks (2) are the most eager to borrow or insure

name: agency costs
definition: the costs incurred by a principal when its agent does not act on its behalf but rather in the agent's own interest

name: agent
definition: an entity enjoined to act on behalf of a principal in some business activity

name: aggregate output
definition: the sum total of all final goods produced in an economy in some period, typically a quarter or a year

name: aggregate output
definition: consumption (C) plus investment (I) plus government spending (G) plus net exports (NX), as in the equation Y = C + I + G + NX

name: amortize
definition: to repay a loan by making interest and partial principal payments each repayment period, typically a month

name: amortization
definition: the process of amortizing a loan

name: annual
definition: year

name: annually
definition: once a year

name: annuitant
definition: the owner or recipient of an annuity

name: annuity
definition: a type of insurance policy that pays the annuitant a sum of money (previously annually but often today monthly) over a pre-specified period or during the annuitant's lifetime or that of his or her spouse

name: ask price
definition: the price at which a dealer will sell a security from its inventory

name: asset
definition: any good owned by any entity and held on its balance sheet

name: asset bubble
definition: the condition when the price of an asset or asset class exceeds its fundamental value for an extended period

name: asset class
definition: a group of similar assets like bonds, equities, or real estate

name: association
definition: any one of a number of types of business entity

name: association
definition: a type of organization

name: asymmetric information
definition: when one party to a contract (buyer or seller) knows more than the counterparty, such as adverse selection, moral hazard, and the principal-agent problem

name: bad
definition: anything that no entity values at greater than zero

name: bad
definition: anything that entities are willing to pay to reduce or eliminate

name: Bagehot's Rule
definition: See Hamilton's Rule

name: balance sheet
definition: a type of financial statement that lists an entity's assets, liabilities, and capital. So called because assets must equal (or in other words be in balance with) liabilities plus capital (which can be negative)

name: balance sheet consolidation
definition: the act of combining the balance sheets of two or more entities, as in a merger

name: bank
definition: one of a variety of financial intermediaries that accepts deposits and makes loans and/or that engages in brokerage, merger and acquisition consulting, or securities issuance

name: bank
definition: to utilize one or more of the services of a bank, particularly to obtain a loan or make a deposit at a depository institution

name: bank of discount and deposit
definition: an archaic term for a commercial bank

name: bank of issue
definition: an archaic term for a bank that issued its own bank notes

name: banker
definition: an individual engaged in banking as a private banker or as an employee of a bank

name: bank notes
definition: a form of paper money issued by banks (banks of issue) and generally convertible into specie at their respective face values at current coin ratings at the bank of issue

name: bank holding company
definition: a bank that holds one or more other banks as assets on its balance sheet

name: bank run
definition: historically, when holders of a bank's demand liabilities, specifically its bank notes or deposits, request payment or conversion en masse

name: bank run
definition: today, when creditors refuse to renew short-term loans to a bank, also known as a silent run

name: banking
definition: the activities of a bank or banker such as making loans, taking deposits, and/or engaging in investment banking

name: bankrupt
definition: an entity in a state of bankruptcy in sense 1 or 2 of that word

name: bankruptcy
definition: generally, the condition of an entity that has negative net worth, to wit the monetary value of its liabilities exceeds the monetary value of its assets.

name: bankruptcy
definition: the state of an entity that has filed for protection from its creditors under a bankruptcy law

name: bankruptcy law
definition: a statute that determines how a bankrupt entity's assets shall be used to pay its liabilities

name: base money
definition: any type of money that banks can count as reserves

name: benefits
definition: the non-monetary compensation of an employee, such as health insurance

name: benefits
definition: more generally, the utility or resources derived by an entity from some good or activity

name: bill
definition: a short-dated bond, especially one issued by the U.S. Treasury

name: bill of credit
definition: a type of medium of exchange or paper money issued by the colonial governments of mainland British North America and often, though not always, made a full legal tender

name: bill of exchange
definition: a short-dated international financial instrument drawn on foreign entity in a foreign currency

name: bid price
definition: the price at which a dealer will buy a security for its inventory

name: bond
definition: generically, any loan

name: bond
definition: in finance, a negotiable, long-dated, interest-bearing financial instrument

name: bondholder
definition: the owner of a bond

name: bondholder
definition: any lender or creditor whose loan is secured by a bond

name: boom
definition: See expansion

name: borrower
definition: any entity that receives principal from a lender in exchange for a promise to repay the principal plus interest in the future

name: branch
definition: an office of an intermediary, typically a bank, where financial services are provided to customers remotely from the financial institution's headquarters

name: broker
definition: any entity that brokers (v.)

name: broker
definition: to match the buyers and sellers of financial instruments in exchange for a commission

name: brokerage
definition: an intermediary that brokers and deals

name: broker-dealer
definition: a brokerage

name: budget deficit
definition: the difference between an entity's (typically a government's) income and its expenditures that must be financed through the sale of assets or the issuance of securities, usually bonds or money

name: business
definition: an entity whose primary goal is to earn profits

name: business
definition: a for-profit firm

name: business
definition: of or pertaining to the activities carried out by businesses

name: business activity
definition: any actions undertaken by any business entity such as buying, selling, brokering, dealing, lending, borrowing, collateralizing, exchanging, or trading

name: business entity
definition: an association, corporation, partnership, sole proprietor, or other entity that buys and/or sells goods in an attempt to earn profits

name: bust
definition: See recession

name: buyer
definition: the entity in a trade that gives up money and receives a non-monetary good in exchange

name: Building and Loan association
definition: a type of mutual corporation that specialized in financing the construction of homes that were replaced following the Great Depression by the Savings and Loan association

name: bullion
definition: gold or silver in the form of bars or ingots

name: call
definition: a demand made for the payment of a liability owed to a creditor

name: call
definition: to demand repayment of a sum due or payable

name: callable
definition: lawfully capable of being called (v.)

name: callable
definition: subject to a call (n.)

name: call loan
definition: a loan, typically an overnight one collateralized by stock, that the lender can call (v.) at any time

name: call option
definition: a type of option derivative that gives the option holder the right but not the obligation to purchase some predetermined asset at a predetermined strike price

name: capital
definition: an entity's net worth

name: capital
definition: the contributions of stockholders to a joint-stock corporation

name: capital
definition: productive physical assets such as factories

name: capitalism
definition: an economic and political system characterized by Lockean government, a modern financial system, open access entrepreneurship, and modern management but also by some level of corruption, rent seeking, and the exploitation of taxpayers and workers

name: capital requirements
definition: capital (1) mandated by some regulator or law, typically expressed as a percentage of a bank's assets

name: cash
definition: any physical medium of exchange that circulates or passes easily hand to hand to make exchanges

name: cash
definition: slang for short-dated commercial paper

name: cash
definition: to convert a financial instrument like a check or a whole life insurance policy into money

name: cash flow
definition: the movement of cash into and out of an entity during some finite period such as a month or a quarter

name: cash value
definition: the sum of money that can be obtained for the relinquishing a whole life insurance policy

name: central bank
definition: a bank established by a government to develop and implement monetary policy and/or act as a lender of last resort during crises and/or regulate financial firms and markets

name: certificate of deposit
definition: a type of time deposit whereby the depositor agrees to pay a penalty if s/he/it withdraws the principal before maturity, a pre-specified date some months or years after making the deposit

name: charter
definition: a statute or special act of incorporation authorizing the creation of a corporation

name: check
definition: a type of draft or written request for payment, typically to a third party, by a depositor in a bank

name: circulation
definition: in the economy, passing from hand to hand as cash

name: circulation
definition: an archaic term that referred to bank notes circulating outside the bank of issue

name: coins
definition: pieces of metal, typically formed into the shape of thin round discs, and embossed with information about its origin (issuer, date of issue, denomination, and so forth)

name: coin rating
definition: the monetary value assigned by governments or other entities to specific specie coins, typically full-bodied

name: collateral
definition: any asset pledged for the repayment of a loan

name: collateralize
definition: to pledge collateral for the repayment of a loan

name: collateralized
definition: backed by collateral

name: commercial bank
definition: a type of bank that primarily makes loans, traditionally discounts, to businesses and that issues mainly checking or other transaction deposits

name: commercial paper
definition: a generic term for any type of short-dated financial instrument, such as a bill of exchange, issued by a business entity

name: commission
definition: a percentage of the sale price of an asset paid to a broker for its brokering services

name: commodity money
definition: cash or media of exchange that derive their liquidity from the monetary value of the commodities, such as copper, silver, or gold, that comprise them

name: commonweal
definition: for the benefit of the community writ large

name: community bank
definition: any relatively small bank that provides financial services to a relatively small geographical area

name: consumption
definition: the use, using, or using up of a good

name: consumption
definition: one of the major components of aggregate output (Y)

name: contract
definition: an agreement, written or oral but typically legally binding, between two or more parties specifying precise terms for the sale or exchange of one or more goods

name: contract
definition: to shrink, as in an economic contraction

name: contract
definition: the act of consummating a contract (n.)

name: conversion
definition: the act of changing (converting) one type of asset into another

name: convertible
definition: subject to being changed (converted) from one type of asset to another

name: convertible bonds
definition: a type of bond that can be changed (converted) into another security, typically an equity

name: convertible money
definition: any type of money that can be changed (converted) into another type of money, such as bank notes into specie

name: copper
definition: a metallic element, symbol Cu and atomic number 29, used to make small denomination full-bodied and token coins

name: corporation
definition: a legal device granting an entity special rights, including, in the case of business entities, perpetual succession, limited liability, and entity shielding

name: corruption
definition: manipulation of the political system by special interests for special interests

name: corruption
definition: the abuse of power by government officials, typically through rent seeking activities such as taking bribes

name: costs
definition: the expenditure of resources, including cash

name: counterparty
definition: the other party to a contract like a derivative or loan

name: country bank
definition: an archaic term for a community bank located in a rural or non-money center (sub)urban area

name: coupon
definition: the physical piece of a coupon bond that bondholders clipped off and presented for payment to the bond's issuer or its redemption agent

name: coupon
definition: an interest payment on a coupon bond

name: coupon bond
definition: specifically, a type of bond upon which interest was paid when the bondholder clipped off a section of the bond called a coupon and presented it to the issuer or its redemption agent

name: coupon bond
definition: generically, any bond that pays interest periodically, such as quarterly or semiannually

name: credit money
definition: any type of money, such as bank notes and deposits, the value of which is dependent on the creditworthiness of the issuer

name: creditor
definition: an entity to which something, typically money, is owed by its debtor

name: credits
definition: generically, an accounting term for things received by an entity, typically stated in terms of its monetary value

name: credits
definition: in banking, a deposit or other payment by a customer to the bank

name: creditworthy
definition: an entity that is thought willing and able to meet all of its current financial obligations

name: creditworthiness
definition: the condition of being creditworthy

name: crisis
definition: See financial crisis

name: currency
definition: cash

name: currency
definition: the prevailing unit of account or coin rating

name: current money
definition: an archaic term for cash

name: credit crunch
definition: a period characterized by a general dearth of liquidity and a decline in the volume of bonds and loans

name: credit union
definition: a type of community bank, depository institution, or thrift owned by its depositors and chartered as a credit union

name: day book
definition: a type of single entry account book that records exchanges on a chronological basis without categorization, much like a cash register roll

name: deal
definition: to offer to buy securities at a bid price and simultaneously offer to sell the same securities at an offer price and profiting from the difference or spread between the two prices

name: dealer
definition: an entity that deals or engages in dealing

name: dealing
definition: the act of buying and selling securities at stated bid and ask prices, respectively

name: debits
definition: generically, an accounting term for things given up by an entity, typically stated in terms of its monetary value

name: debits
definition: in banking, a loan or other payment by a bank to a customer

name: debt
definition: anything owed to another entity, typically money

name: debt instrument
definition: any of a variety of financial instruments representing a debt such as an IOU

name: debtor
definition: an entity which owes something, typically money, to its creditor

name: default
definition: the failure of an issuer or other lender to make one or more contractual payments of principal or interest due on a bond or other debt instrument

name: default
definition: to fail to make a payment due on a bond or other debt instrument

name: default risk
definition: the probability of default (n.)

name: demand
definition: the quantity of a good that buyers desire to purchase at any given price

name: demand
definition: a request for immediate payment or conversion

name: demand
definition: to request a payment or conversion that has fallen due

name: demand liabilities
definition: liabilities that lenders can call (demand the payment of) on demand (n., 2, no or short notice)

name: denomination
definition: the face value of a bank note, bill of credit, or coin

name: depositor
definition: an entity that owns a bank deposit

name: depository institution
definition: any type of bank that issues deposits, including Building and Loan associations, commercial banks, credit unions, mutual savings banks, Savings and Loan associations, savings banks, and universal banks but not investment banks

name: deposit
definition: a sum owed by a bank to a depositor

name: deposit
definition: to create any variety of a deposit (n.) in a bank by placing money at its disposal or by obtaining a loan from it

name: derivative
definition: a financial instrument the monetary value of which is linked to the price of some underlying asset

name: direct public offering
definition: an offering of shares in itself by a business entity to members of the public directly, to wit without the services of an investment bank or other intermediary

name: discount
definition: a type of loan whereby a bank or other lender pays the borrower the discounted present value of a promissory note or bill of exchange in exchange for the right to collect the face value of the discounted instrument at its maturity

name: discount
definition: to make a discount loan by paying the discounted present value of a financial instrument in exchange for the right to collect its face value at its maturity

name: discounted present value
definition: is the price (present value) of an asset determined by the formula PV (price) equals FV (future value or face value) divided by one plus the interest rate. Note that for any interest rate greater than zero the equation will yield a price less than the face value. The difference between the face value and current price is the time value of money

name: dishonor
definition: an archaic term meaning to default (v.)

name: disintermediation
definition: the process or condition of reducing exchanges between borrowers and lenders

name: double entry
definition: a method of keeping accounts that is more sophisticated than single entry because it involves describing both the credit and debit aspect of each exchange

name: draft
definition: a written request for payment, typically to a third party, drawn by a creditor of the payer

name: drawee
definition: the entity being drawn upon by a drawer or putative creditor

name: drawee
definition: the acceptor

name: drawee
definition: the payer

name: drawer
definition: the entity drawing on its money in the possession of its putative debtor or drawee

name: draw on
definition: to formally request a putative debtor to make payment per the terms specified in a check, draft, or bill of exchange

name: economic contraction
definition: See recession

name: economic history
definition: the study of past states of the economy using the analytical tools of economists and the source material of historians

name: economics
definition: the social science devoted to the study of the economy, especially the production and consumption of goods

name: economists
definition: individuals who study economics

name: economy
definition: the sum total of all the interactions of entities in markets at any given time

name: entity
definition: a firm, government, individual, organization, or business entity

name: entity
definition: an economic unit of production and/or consumption

name: entity shielding
definition: a privilege that protects the assets of corporations from seizure by the creditors of bankrupt owners, typically stockholders

name: entrepreneur
definition: generally, any entity that attempts to increase its utility by innovating

name: entrepreneur
definition: an individual who establishes a new business entity

name: entrepreneur
definition: a business entity that attempts to invent a new good, develop a new market, introduce a new method of production or distribution, discover a new source of supply, reorganize an existing industry, or engage in rent-seeking

name: entrepreneurship
definition: the state or condition of being an entrepreneur

name: equity
definition: a share in a corporation

name: equity
definition: net worth

name: equity market
definition: a market where equities or shares are exchanged

name: exchange
definition: the process of engaging in exchange (v.)

name: exchange
definition: a physical location for trading securities

name: exchange
definition: an entity than maintains an exchange (2)

name: exchange
definition: to give one thing for another, typically money for a non-monetary good

name: expansion
definition: a state of the economy during which aggregate output, typically as measured by Gross Domestic Product, increases past all previous levels

name: expenditures
definition: money that flows out of one entity and, typically, into another

name: exploitation
definition: the stealing of resources from another, typically weaker, entity

name: exports
definition: goods produced domestically but consumed abroad or consumed by foreign entities domestically (e.g. tourism)

name: externalities
definition: a type of market failure created when prices do not reflect the full costs or benefits of a good to society

name: face value
definition: the monetary value expressed on (the face of) a financial instrument, bank note, or coin

name: Federal Reserve System
definition: the U.S. central bank established in 1913 and still in operation today

name: Federal Reserve Notes
definition: fiat paper money issued by the Federal Reserve System

name: fiat money
definition: a type of non-commodity money, typically made of paper or token coins, that derives its value from legal tender provisions

name: fiat money
definition: fiduciary money

name: fiduciary money
definition: a type of non-commodity money composed of substances with a monetary value far below the face value of the fiduciary note or coin that derives its value from the public's belief that they will be able to exchange the money at its face value due to its current widespread acceptance

name: fiduciary money
definition: fiat money

name: final goods
definition: goods that are consumed or invested and not used in the production of other goods

name: finance
definition: the science of managing assets, including money

name: finance
definition: to obtain the money necessary to attempt completion of some project

name: financial condition
definition: the overall status of an entity's assets, liabilities, equity (capital), income, and cash flow at any given time

name: financial crisis
definition: a period characterized by rapid reductions in the monetary value of financial assets and the market capitalization of financial institutions and, typically, non-financial entities as well

name: financial guarantee
definition: a type of financial obligation whereby the guarantor or surety promises to pay some third party if a guaranteed entity defaults on its debt or otherwise fails to perform according to contract

name: financial industry
definition: the sum of all business entities serving any financial market

name: financial institution
definition: narrowly, a business entity that provides financial service(s)

name: financial institution
definition: broadly, any business or government entity involved in any way in any financial market

name: financial instrument
definition: any variety of financial contract, including cash, bond, equity, or derivative

name: financial market
definition: any market for any financial instrument or financial service

name: financial obligations
definition: anything owed, owing, or potential owing, such as liabilities, endorsements, and financial guarantees

name: financial panic
definition: a period characterized by the panicked selling of assets to increase the reserves of banks or the cash balances of other types of entities. See Panic of 1792

name: financial service
definition: any of a range of services related to financial instruments, derivatives, insurance, money, intermediation, or any other financial good

name: financial statement
definition: a generic term for any type of account of any entity's financial condition, including balance sheets and income and cash flow statements

name: financial system
definition: all financial institutions and markets and their multifarious interconnections

name: financier
definition: a banker or other individual who provides one or more financial services on behalf of himself/herself or a bank, broker, or other intermediary

name: firm
definition: any business entity

name: firm
definition: a small or private business entity such as a sole proprietorship or partnership, as in a law firm

name: for profit
definition: an organization, typically a business entity, with the common goal of earning a profit

name: forward contract
definition: singular version of forwards

name: forwards
definition: a type of derivative whereby a buyer and seller agree to exchange a specific quantity of some asset or other good at a future date for predetermined price

name: free ride
definition: to enjoy the benefits of a good without paying for it

name: free rider
definition: any entity that free rides

name: full-bodied coins
definition: specie

name: full-bodied coins
definition: coins that derive their monetary value from the intrinsic value of the gold, silver, copper (or occasionally other metal) they contain rather than from a legal tender provision; non-token coins

name: fundamental value
definition: the rational value of an asset based on its intrinsic characteristics and interest rates

name: future value
definition: the principal, par value, or face value of a bond or other debt instrument, so called because that is the monetary sum promised to be paid in the future

name: futures
definition: a type of derivative, specifically a forward contract that has been standardized and trades on an exchange

name: gold
definition: a metallic element with symbol Au and atomic number 79 used, among other things, to create full-bodied and token coins

name: good
definition: a product or service that someone values greater than zero, that people are willing to pay in order to obtain

name: government bond
definition: a bond issued by a national or municipal (sub-national) government

name: government expenditure
definition: money spent by the government on final goods (i.e., not simply redistributed to citizens via Social Security or other social programs)

name: government expenditure
definition: one of the major components of aggregate output (Y)

name: government failure
definition: the inability of a government to meet one or more of its goals due to its own inadequacy

name: gross domestic product
definition: one of the most widely used estimates of aggregate output (Y)

name: Hamilton's Rule
definition: a rule developed by Treasury Secretary Alexander Hamilton (1755-1804) during the Panic of 1792 that instructs central banks or other lenders of last resort to lend freely at a penalty rate of interest to any entity that can post sufficient collateral

name: health insurance
definition: an insurance policy that indemnifies policyholders if a covered event, such as an illness or hospitalization, occurs while the policy is in effect

name: history of economic thought
definition: the study of past beliefs of economists

name: honor
definition: archaic term meaning to make payment

name: human capital
definition: the ability of individuals to create goods

name: hybrid corporation
definition: a corporation that is partly owned by stockholders and partly by customers

name: hybrid corporation
definition: a corporation that is part joint-stock and part mutual

name: hybrid failures
definition: intricate combinations of market failures and government failures

name: illiquid
definition: the condition of an asset that cannot be sold in timely manner at or close to its fundamental value

name: illiquidity
definition: the state of being illiquid

name: imports
definition: goods produced abroad but consumed domestically or purchased abroad by citizens of the importing nation (e.g. tourism)

name: income
definition: money that is incoming, that flows into an entity

name: indemnify
definition: to compensate for a damage or loss actually incurred

name: inflation
definition: sustained increases in the price level

name: initial public offering
definition: an offering of shares in itself by a business entity to members of the public with the aid of an investment bank or other intermediary

name: in-kind loan
definition: the lending of a specific good rather than of money

name: inland bill
definition: a short-dated financial instrument drawn on a domestic entity

name: insolvency
definition: the inability of an entity to pay legitimate demands on it, either from bankruptcy or illiquidity

name: insurance
definition: a mechanism for spreading risks, typically in an actuarially or scientifically sound manner, through the issuance of insurance policies

name: insurance agent
definition: an agent hired by an insurance company or other insurer to sell its insurance policies and to provide basic customer service

name: insurance company
definition: a business entity, typically in the form of a corporation, that acts as an insurer

name: insurance policy
definition: a contract specifying the terms upon which an insurer promises to indemnify the policyholder or insured for some loss

name: insured
definition: the entity reimbursed when/if some contingency specified in an insurance policy occurs

name: insurer
definition: the issuer of an insurance policy

name: instrument
definition: a financial instrument

name: instrument
definition: a monetary policy tool

name: interest
definition: the opportunity cost of money

name: interest
definition: a rental charge for the use of money

name: interest-only loan
definition: a loan in which the borrower repays no principal, only interest, forever (perpetuity) or for some pre-specified period

name: interest rate
definition: the interest (promised or received) over some period, typically a year, divided by the principal of a bond or other loan, generally expressed as a percentage

name: interest rate
definition: yield

name: intermediary
definition: any entity, but typically a business entity, that brokers exchanges between lenders and borrowers

name: intermediation
definition: the function of an intermediary

name: intermediation
definition: the process of brokering exchanges between borrowers and lenders

name: investment
definition: an asset purchased by an investor with the aim of earning a profit

name: investment
definition: a major component of aggregate output (Y) that measures purchases of machines, factories, and inventory by businesses (I)

name: investment bank
definition: a type of bank owned and/or run by investment bankers that engages in brokerage, issuance of securities, and merger and acquisition consulting

name: investment banker
definition: a banker primarily engaged in brokerage, issuance of securities, and merger and acquisition consulting

name: investment banking
definition: the activities of an investment banker

name: investor
definition: an entity that intends to earn a profit by buying, holding, or selling a financial instrument such as a bond or equity

name: IOU
definition: a short-dated debt instrument, like a promissory note, so called because "I owe you."

name: issuance
definition: the act of issuing

name: issue
definition: a thing, typically a bank note, coin, deposit, insurance policy, or security, issued

name: issue
definition: to emit, put into circulation, or put into effect

name: issuer
definition: any entity that issues (v.) any type of issue (n.)

name: joint-stock company
definition: an unincorporated or unchartered business entity owned by stockholders

name: joint-stock corporation
definition: a type of corporation owned by stockholders

name: journal
definition: a type of double-entry account book that tracks transactions chronologically first, then by category

name: ledger
definition: a type of double-entry account book that tracks transactions by category first, then chronologically within each category

name: legal tender
definition: an obligation created and enforced by governments on entities to accept a specific medium of exchange at its face value in either a) all debts public and private (full tender) or b) all public debts (public tender)

name: legal tender
definition: any medium of exchange that enjoys full legal tender status

name: lemons problem
definition: a famous example of adverse selection and asymmetric information wherein buyers of used vehicles pay too much for unreliable automobiles, trucks, and so forth

name: lender
definition: any entity that provides principal to a borrower in exchange for repayment of the principal plus interest in the future

name: lender of last resort
definition: a central bank or other monetary authority charged with lending to entities in the wake of a financial crisis or panic when other sources of loans are less or completely unavailable due to high degrees of risk and/or uncertainty

name: liability run
definition: when depositors, lenders, or other creditors call or refuse to renew loans to an entity, such as a bank

name: liabilities
definition: anything owed by one entity to another

name: life insurance
definition: an insurance policy that indemnifies a policyholder or beneficiary if a covered event, such as the death of the insured, occurs when the policy is in effect

name: limited liability
definition: a common feature in charters that protects stockholders' personal wealth in the event of the corporation's bankruptcy

name: liquid
definition: the condition of an asset that can be easily or quickly sold for cash at close to its monetary value

name: liquidity
definition: the state of being liquid

name: liquidity
definition: cash issued by a central bank or other monetary authority to render assets more liquid

name: loan
definition: a type of contract whereby a borrower promises to repay to a lender the principal sum borrowed plus interest

name: Lockean government
definition: a government ostensibly dedicated to the protection of the lives, liberty, and property of its citizenry

name: long-dated
definition: having more than a year to maturity but not a perpetuity

name: loss
definition: the sale of an asset at less than its purchase price

name: loss
definition: diminution of the monetary value of an asset for which indemnification from an insurer on an insurance policy is sought

name: loss
definition: the negative difference between a business entity's total revenues and its total costs

name: Madisonian constitution
definition: a frame of government that limits tyranny through the use of checks and balances or the diffusion of power over multiple branches or levels of government

name: management
definition: all of the managers of an entity

name: management
definition: the art and science of efficiently operating large, complex organizations, especially joint-stock corporations

name: manager
definition: an individual charged with administering, running, or operating a business entity or organization

name: market capitalization
definition: the monetary value of a corporation calculated by multiplying the price of one of its shares by the total number of shares outstanding

name: market failure
definition: the inability of a market to achieve one or more of its goals due to its own inadequacy

name: market power
definition: (no definition provided in source)

name: markets
definition: wherever or how ever entities exchange goods at prices determined primarily by supply and demand

name: maturity
definition: the date when a debt instrument's principal falls due and needs to be paid lest a default be declared

name: media of exchange
definition: anything that circulates hand to hand as cash money

name: merger
definition: the balance sheet consolidation of two business entities, typically of similar size, the result of which is a new, larger entity

name: monetary authority
definition: the central bank, currency board, or other government agency charged with developing and implementing a nation's monetary policy, including the money supply and interest rates

name: monetary policy
definition: the actions of monetary authorities, such as central banks, designed to influence the money supply and interest rates

name: monetary value
definition: the price or worth of something in terms of money, as opposed to use value

name: money
definition: physical media of exchange

name: money
definition: abstract unit of account

name: money
definition: long-term store of value

name: money of account
definition: monetary values represented in account books

name: money supply
definition: the total monetary value of all the money in actual circulation or use in an economy

name: moral hazard
definition: (no definition provided in source)

name: mortgage
definition: a type of loan wherein the borrower pledges real estate as collateral

name: municipal bond
definition: a type of government bond issued by a sub-national government such as a state, county, or city

name: mutual corporation
definition: a type of for profit business corporation owned by its customers, typically its depositors or policyholders

name: mutual savings bank
definition: a type of savings bank or thrift owned by its depositors but not chartered as a credit union

name: negative equity
definition: when the net worth of an entity is less than zero. Indicative of bankruptcy or insolvency

name: negative externalities
definition: a market failure that occurs when the full costs of a good are not incorporated in its price, as in the case, for example, of pollution

name: negotiable
definition: transferable from one entity to another by sale, gift, inheritance, or other means

name: negotiable certificate of deposit
definition: a large denomination certificate of deposit that can be bought and sold like a bond

name: net exports
definition: the monetary value of exports minus the monetary value of imports

name: net worth
definition: the sum of the monetary value of an entity's assets and liabilities

name: nominal price
definition: the price of a good in current dollars

name: nominal price
definition: prices of goods not adjusted for changes in the price level

name: non-profit
definition: an organization that is designed not to earn any profits

name: not-for-profit
definition: an organization that may earn profits but that is not primarily oriented toward doing so

name: opportunity cost
definition: the inevitable cost incurred by entities when they choose an activity, thereby precluding the completion of another activity at the same time

name: option holder
definition: the owner of one or more options

name: option contract
definition: See options

name: options
definition: a class of derivatives including call options and put options

name: organization
definition: a group of individuals working closely together towards a common goal

name: over-the-counter
definition: any market for trading securities outside of a formal exchange, typically coordinated by brokers and/or dealers

name: owe
definition: to be obliged to repay, usually a sum of money

name: owe
definition: to possess but not have legal title of ownership of

name: own
definition: to possess

name: own
definition: to have legal title to or the legal right to sell, lease, or enjoy

name: owner
definition: an entity that owns a business entity or asset

name: ownership
definition: the state or condition of owning (v.)

name: panic
definition: See financial panic

name: Panic of 1792
definition: a financial panic that originated in the government bond market that was successfully thwarted by the application of Hamilton's Rule

name: Panic of 1819
definition: a financial panic that led to a deep recession and a re-alignment of U.S. political parties

name: Panic of 1837
definition: a financial panic that led to a long, deep recession

name: paper money
definition: a generic term for any type of money composed of paper, including fiat monies and convertible monies such as bank notes

name: partners
definition: the individuals who own a partnership

name: partnership
definition: a type of business entity owned by two or more individuals called partners

name: payer
definition: the entity upon which a draft is drawn, typically the drawer's debtor

name: perpetual succession
definition: a privilege of corporations to change their owners/stockholders without having to reconstitute, as partnerships traditionally had to do whenever a partner joined or left the business entity

name: perpetuity
definition: a financial instrument with no maturity date

name: perpetuity
definition: an interest-only loan

name: personal estate
definition: any asset owned by an individual that is not real estate

name: policyholder
definition: the owner of an insurance contract

name: positive externalities
definition: a market failure that occurs when the full societal benefits of a good are not incorporated in its price, as in the case, for example, of education

name: premiums
definition: the price a policyholder must pay to effect an insurance contract

name: present value
definition: the price of an asset or other good today (at the present)

name: price
definition: the amount of compensation or payment a buyer gives the seller in exchange for a good; also, the monetary value of a good determined by the interaction of supply and demand in a market

name: price level
definition: the average of all nominal prices in an economy

name: principal
definition: a sum lent or invested upon which interest or rate of return are calculated

name: principal
definition: the, or one of the, owners of an entity

name: principal-agent problem
definition: a specific type of moral hazard that occurs when an agent acts in its own best interest rather than in the interest of the owner(s)

name: private bank
definition: a bank operating without a charter

name: private bank
definition: a bank that manages the assets of wealthy entities, typically individuals

name: private banker
definition: an individual or a member of a partnership in an unchartered bank, i.e., private bank (1)

name: private banker
definition: a banker in a private bank

name: product
definition: a physical thing or contract that a business entity creates, produces, makes, manufactures, or grows

name: profit
definition: the positive difference between a business entity's total revenues and its total costs

name: promissory note
definition: a short-dated negotiable debt instrument such as an IOU

name: primary reserves
definition: See reserves

name: project
definition: any specific task aimed at achieving a goal

name: project
definition: in business, any specific actions taken in an attempt to earn a profit

name: public company
definition: a business entity that is owned by private individuals (members of the public), typically stockholders who can trade their equity stakes in the company publically

name: public company
definition: a joint-stock company or corporation

name: public goods
definition: a market failure that arises when it is not in the interest of any business entity to supply a specific good, like national defense, because the entity cannot easily profit from its provision because such goods are non-excludable (there is no way to force free riders to pay) and non-rivalrous (consumption by one does not prevent consumption by others)

name: put option
definition: a type of option derivative that gives the option holder the right but not the obligation to sell some predetermined asset at a predetermined strike price

name: quarter
definition: a quarter of a year or three months, typically January, February, March; April, May, June; July, August, September; October, November, December

name: quarterly
definition: once every quarter

name: rate of interest
definition: See interest rate

name: rate of return
definition: the ratio of the money lost or gained on an investment relative to the principal invested over some period, typically a quarter or year

name: rate of return
definition: return on investment (ROI)

name: recovery
definition: a state of the economy following a recession during which aggregate output, typically as measured by Gross Domestic Product, increases toward a previous peak

name: real estate
definition: a type of asset consisting of land and any improvements thereto, such as buildings, drainage or sewage systems, roads, wells, and so forth

name: real price
definition: the price of a good adjusted for changes in the price level

name: recession
definition: a state of the economy during which aggregate output, typically as measured by Gross Domestic Product, declines

name: regulated firm
definition: a business entity that is subject to the regulations of one or more regulators

name: regulations
definition: a set of rules prescribed by a regulator describing the business activities that can and/or cannot lawfully be undertaken by a business entity

name: regulator
definition: an entity, usually a government, that makes and/or enforces regulations

name: regulatory capture
definition: the condition of a regulated firm taking control of its regulator in whole or part

name: relative prices
definition: the ratio of the nominal price of one good to the nominal price of another

name: rent seeking
definition: attempts to gain something for nothing by manipulating the government to subsidize or otherwise support special interests at the expense of the commonweal

name: required reserves
definition: See reserve requirements

name: reserves
definition: cash held by banks to meet calls on their demand liabilities, such as checking deposits and bank notes

name: reserves
definition: any asset that banks own to help manage their liquidity

name: reserve requirements
definition: reserves mandated by some regulator or law, typically expressed as a percentage of a bank's demand liabilities

name: resources
definition: goods, such as copper, gold, silver, oil, diamonds, created by nature rather than by entities

name: resources
definition: in a loose sense, any asset or good, including more intangible ones like time

name: returns
definition: money that returns to an investor on an investment

name: revenues
definition: income from any source, including the sale of goods or returns on investments

name: risk
definition: known volatility in the rate of return

name: risk appetite
definition: the amount of risk an investor can tolerate

name: risk averse
definition: avoidance of risk even at a high cost

name: risk aversion
definition: the practice of being risk averse

name: risks
definition: the risk represented by an entity seeking a loan or insurance

name: risks
definition: the entity itself

name: risky
definition: characterized by excessive risk, either for the expected rate of return or for the investor's risk appetite

name: Savings and Loan association
definition: a type of savings bank with a Savings and Loan charter designed to modernize the older Building and Loan association form

name: savings bank
definition: a generic term for any bank that focuses on making mortgage loans and issuing savings deposits, including but not limited to credit unions, mutual savings banks, and Savings and Loan associations

name: savings deposit
definition: a type of time deposit in a bank that earns interest in exchange for a decrease in its liquidity

name: secondary reserves
definition: a sort of back up form of reserves held by banks that earns income but is liquid (readily convertible into cash)

name: securities
definition: any negotiable financial instrument, including debt, equity, and hybrid instruments

name: securities exchange
definition: See exchange

name: seller
definition: the entity in a trade that gives up a non-monetary good and receives money in exchange

name: semiannually
definition: twice a year or every six months

name: service
definition: a good consumed at the point of contact with the service provider including but not limited to consulting, education, healthcare, and retail

name: share
definition: a financial instrument representing an ownership or equity stake in a joint-stock corporation

name: share
definition: an equity

name: shareholder
definition: See stockholder

name: short
definition: to sell an asset under the expectation of buying it back later at a lower price

name: short
definition: borrowing assets, typically equities, selling them in the expectation of a price decrease, then buying them back later to repay the in-kind loan

name: short
definition: having fewer shares (or other assets) than necessary to repay the in-kind loan taken at the start of a shorting operation, as in the expression "caught short."

name: short-dated
definition: having less than a year to maturity

name: short sale
definition: traditionally, a transaction whereby an entity shorts an asset

name: short sale
definition: more recently, the sale of a home for less than the outstanding mortgage balance

name: shorting
definition: the process of making a short sale

name: sight draft
definition: a draft due upon its acceptance for payment by the payer

name: silent run
definition: a type of bank run or liability run characterized by the refusal of creditors to renew short-term loans to a bank or other entity

name: silver
definition: a metallic element with the symbol Ag and the atomic number 47 used to create full-bodied and token coins

name: single entry
definition: a simple method of keeping accounts that entails listing the major attributes (e.g., date, price, counterparty) of exchanges

name: sole proprietor
definition: the owner of a sole proprietorship

name: sole proprietorship
definition: a type of business entity owned and operated by a single individual

name: sovereign bond
definition: a government bond issued by a sovereign national government

name: special interests
definition: entities that engage in rent seeking or other activities designed to subsidize them at the expense of others, or the common weal

name: specialty
definition: a type of contract where the parties agree that payment will be made in a specific medium of exchange, such as gold or silver

name: specie
definition: full-bodied (i.e., non-token) gold or silver coins

name: speculate
definition: to engage in speculation

name: speculation
definition: an attempt to earn quick profits by buying assets, typically securities, low and selling them high or vice versa, as in shorting

name: spread
definition: the difference between a dealer's bid price and its ask price for a security

name: spread
definition: the difference between what a bank receives for its assets and pays for its liabilities

name: stock
definition: synonymous with equity (1) and share (1)

name: stock
definition: archaic for government bond

name: stock exchange
definition: See exchange

name: stock market
definition: exchange (n.)

name: stock market
definition: any market in which stocks are traded, including exchanges but also over-the-counter or broker-dealer markets

name: stock market crash
definition: a type of financial crisis characterized by rapid decreases in the prices of a broad swath of equities

name: stockholder
definition: an owner of one or more shares (stocks, equities) in a joint-stock corporation

name: stockjobbing
definition: buying and selling securities in order to speculate

name: stockjobber
definition: an archaic term for any entity that engages in stockjobbing

name: store of value
definition: any asset that maintains most or all of its monetary value over long periods of time, e.g. years

name: strike price
definition: the predetermined price at which an option derivative can be contractually exercised by the option holder

name: swap
definition: a type of derivative whereby two parties exchange one asset for another on an on-going basis according to the value of some underlying asset, for example dollars for yen

name: subsidize
definition: to grant a subsidy to an entity

name: subsidy
definition: resources, typically but not always money, given to an entity, usually by a government

name: sunk costs
definition: costs that have already been incurred and cannot be recouped

name: supply
definition: the quantity of a good that sellers make available at any given price

name: suspension of specie payments
definition: when banks of issue ceased converting their bank notes and deposits into specie due to their bankruptcy, insolvency, or a general suspension of payments in times of war or financial panic

name: term life
definition: an insurance policy that indemnifies a policyholder or beneficiary if the insured dies during the duration (term) of the contract

name: thrift
definition: a depository institution with a community bank focus such as credit unions and savings banks

name: time deposit
definition: a type of deposit, like a savings deposit or a certificate of deposit, that cannot be withdrawn by the depositor until a specified period has elapsed or a penalty had been paid

name: time draft
definition: a draft due some days, weeks, or months after its acceptance for payment by the payer

name: token coinage
definition: a type of fiat money that takes the form of coins that contain metals worth considerably less than the coin's face value

name: trade
definition: an exchange of goods, typically between two entities

name: trade
definition: to engage in a trade

name: transaction deposits
definition: See checking deposits

name: Treasury bill
definition: a short-dated sovereign bond issued by the U.S. Treasury to help manage the U.S. government's cash flow needs

name: Treasury bond
definition: a sovereign bond issued by the U.S. Treasury to fund U.S. government budget deficits

name: unbanked
definition: entities, typically individuals, who do not bank (v.)

name: uncertainty
definition: unknown/unknowable volatility in the rate of return

name: underlying asset
definition: an asset that contractually determines the price of another asset

name: unit bank
definition: a bank that does not, probably because it lawfully cannot, operate any branches

name: unit of account
definition: the abstract measuring rod against which monetary values are determined

name: unit of account
definition: money of account

name: universal bank
definition: a type of bank that combines the functions of a depository institution with those of an investment bank

name: usance
definition: the period between the issuance or acceptance of a financial instrument, such as a bill of exchange, and its maturity or due date

name: use value
definition: the worth or utility of a good stemming from its actual utilization or consumption

name: utility
definition: an economic concept measuring an entity's relative satisfaction with a good

name: whole life
definition: a life insurance policy that indemnifies a policyholder or beneficiary when the insured dies, if the policy is current or has been paid up, and that can be cashed or borrowed against using the cash value of the policy as collateral

name: yield
definition: the current yield, or the income (typically the annual dividends or coupons) from some investment divided by the investment's current price

name: yield
definition: the yield to maturity or discounted cash flow rate of return
